headline: Land grabs and extortion take new turn in Dhaka with mob attacks, police stand by
summary: A troubling new pattern of organized mob violence, vandalism, and looting has emerged in Dhaka, targeting properties and construction sites across the capital.
details: Four attacks in just three days involving land disputes, land grabs, vandalism, and looting have brought a troubling new pattern into focus in Dhaka.
These incidents saw dozens, sometimes hundreds, of people joining the attacks. Heavy machinery, including bulldozers, was used in at least one case to raze structures to the ground.

While land grabbing and extortion are not new to the capital, fresh concern is igniting over the organized nature of these latest incidents. Groups are arriving together, forcing their way onto properties, vandalizing structures, and removing valuables.

Specific incidents include the demolition of the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur, an attack on an office in Chand Udyan in Mohammadpur, an assault on a building in Shekhertek in Adabar, and an attack on a New Gini Properties project in Manikdi.

Allegations of involvement by leaders and activists of the ruling party have surfaced in some cases. Despite police arrests and the Home Minister's assurance that "No criminal will be spared," victims report a surge in extortion and land grabbing.

Buildings under construction have become routine targets for demands for money. Site engineer Ismail Howlader noted, "The boys have understood that there’s big money in land. Now they’re just looking for an opportunity."

Victims state that land-related extortion has reached alarming levels in rapidly developing areas like Mirpur and Mohammadpur. Privately owned plots and buildings under construction are now widely targeted, with demands even made for rubble removal.

One banker, who wished to remain anonymous for safety, recounted how he and partners built an eight-storey structure on their own plot, only to be driven away by 40-50 alleged extortionists. They had invested their lifetime savings.

He lamented, "There is no law in this country. There is no police." For six months, they have been unable to access their property, fearing for their lives, despite completing the eighth floor's roof.

Diploma engineer Ismail Howlader, with years of experience in Mohammadpur and Adabar, confirms that pressure and interference at construction sites have become increasingly common, with people causing trouble at any time.

headline: Bangladesh Missions abroad face visa delays due to technical issues with central DIP server
summary: Technical glitches with the Department of Immigration and Passports' central system have halted MRV and NVR processing, causing significant inconvenience for applicants worldwide.
details: Bangladesh Missions abroad are experiencing significant delays in visa and NVR processing due to technical issues with the central system of the Department of Immigration and Passports (DIP). The Machine Readable Visa (MRV) server is currently unavailable, impacting services globally.

A senior official confirmed that efforts are underway to resolve the technical issues as soon as possible. All missions abroad are facing the same problem, leading to temporary disruptions in service.

Visa applicants, including one from a European country, reported submitting applications online but receiving no further communication or responses to calls. The system, which usually promises an email within 24 hours, has failed to deliver.

The government has requested applicants to allow additional time for processing and to avoid repeated inquiries regarding the status of their applications. Embassies, including those in Berlin and Bangkok, have issued urgent notices regretting the inconvenience.

Missions abroad will inform applicants via their websites and Facebook pages once the central system is restored and normal visa services resume. Applicants are advised to bear with the temporary inconvenience and avoid making urgent travel arrangements dependent on immediate visa processing.
